explanations: run() flushes the batcher before it waits for in-flight requests to finish. A request that was already past the 'accepting' check when SIGTERM arrived finishes afterwards: it adds its readings to the batcher's buffer and answers 202. But the flush has already happened, and the process exits with those readings still in memory. Shutdown has to go in dependency order: stop accepting, wait for in-flight requests to drain, then flush what they buffered, then close the sink. Moving the flush after the drain makes every 202 durable before exit.
